Integrate Baltic Germans: The Baltic Germans have lived alongside us for centuries, contributing heavily to our local administration and economy. By formally integrating them into our state apparatus, we can harness their expertise and smooth over historical tensions.
Organize the Üldlaulupidu

The Estonian Song Festival is a cornerstone of our national awakening. By organizing this massive gathering in Tartu, we will unite the Estonian people through song and solidify our cultural identity on the world stage.
Hold the Laulupidu
Five years have passed, and the song grounds of Tartu call again. Tens of thousands of voices in one choir will carry the republic's name to the world and its people closer to each other.
Publish the Kalevipoeg

Compiled by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald, the Kalevipoeg is our national epic. Publishing this work will cement the Estonian language in literature and inspire romantic nationalism among our populace.
Found the Estonian Students' Society
The establishment of the Eesti Üliõpilaste Selts (EÜS) will provide an intellectual bedrock for our national movement. Their blue, black, and white tricolor will soon become the symbol of our people.
Work the Põlevkivi Reserves

Vast beds of oil shale - põlevkivi, the burning stone - lie beneath Ida-Viru. With the new chemistry of clean coal, the shale can be worked as a low-grade coal: fuel for the railways, the mills and the ports of Narva.
Enact the Land Reform (Maareform)

For centuries, Baltic German nobles have controlled the vast majority of our arable land. Maaseadus will expropriate these manor estates and distribute the land to the Estonian peasantry, breaking aristocratic power forever.
Expand the Baltic Railway
Investing heavily in the Balti Raudtee will connect our major cities and ports, drastically improving infrastructure and paving the way for heavy industrialization.
Found the Kaitseliit
In times of crisis, the regular army is not enough. Forming the voluntary Defence League (Kaitseliit) will provide us with a paramilitary force ready to defend the homeland at a moment's notice.
Sign the Treaty of Tartu

With our independence secured, we have signed a historic peace treaty. Russia, weakened and no longer among the great powers, has renounced all claims to our territory for all time and compensated us with a substantial sum of gold rubles from their imperial reserves.
Enact the Era of Silence (Vaikiv Ajastu)

With veterans marching in the streets and the constitution deadlocked, the executive declares an emergency state of defense. Political assemblies and partisan activity are suspended, ushering in the 'Era of Silence' - state authority consolidated at the expense of parliamentary democracy.
Propose the Baltic Entente
As a rising power in the region, Estonia is well-positioned to lead a diplomatic bloc. By bringing Latvia and Lithuania into our sphere, we can form a united Baltic front against foreign aggression.
The Baltic Schooling Tradition

Centuries of Lutheran parish schooling, confirmation reading requirements, and the academic presence of the Imperial University of Dorpat have left the population of Estland and Livland far more literate than the imperial norm.

Armored Trains
By mounting naval guns and machine guns on armored rail carriages, our army can project heavy firepower anywhere the Baltic railway network reaches. Where the rails run, the soomusrong follows.
The Soomusrong

Our engineers have bolted guns and armor onto railway carriages to create the soomusrong - the armored train. On the broad-gauge rails of the Baltic, these iron beasts can carry heavy firepower wherever the army needs it, striking deep and fast along the lines.

Retort the Põlevkivi into Shale Oil

The pits of Ida-Viru already yield burning stone by the wagonload. Now the retorts of inorganic chemistry can cook the shale into oil, and Narva becomes a fountain of fuel for the modern age. Yet the retorts belch their ash over the parish, and the water turns dark: progress carries a price in land and peace alike.
Open the Maardu Phosphorite Pits

Beneath the thin soils east of Tallinn lie the pale beds of phosphorite - the promise of superphosphate for fields across the Baltic. With the new organic chemistry, the fertilizer of the future can be cooked from stone. The pits will scar the land at Maardu and poison its wells, and the farmers will not suffer the dust and blasting in silence - but the harvests of a hundred farms will rise from them.
